sermon.title: Did They Live It?
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer asks whether the apostles lived up to Romans 8—nothing can separate us—and shows from Paul’s sufferings that they did. He gives five reasons: a personal encounter with Jesus, Jesus praying for them, ongoing conversion, opened understanding and the power of the Holy Ghost. With the word and the gifts of the Spirit they turned a hostile world upside down, and he says the church can do the same in America.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: Paul’s “40 stripes less one” spoken as “15 times”; John “tarred and feathered” and Bartholomew flayed (tradition); “a hundred and eight more” at Pentecost; “15 different languages”; Mark 16:20 spoken as “Matthew 16:20”; Dorcas raised by “Paul” (Peter in Acts 9); “Peter and Barnabas” at Lystra (Paul and Barnabas); Constantine dated “390 AD”; “them” called added in Mark 16:20. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Jews killed Jesus (with all sinners responsible); corrupt government in DC; Democrats and Republicans; liberals and political correctness; evangelicals can sway any election.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And in Lystra a certain man without strength in his feet was sitting, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who had never walked. This man heard Paul speaking. Paul, observing him intently and seeing that he had faith to be healed, said with a loud voice, “Stand up straight on your feet!” And he leaped and walked.
And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke.

And when Simon saw that through the laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Spirit was given, he offered them money, saying, “Give me this power also, that anyone on whom I lay hands may receive the Holy Spirit.” But Peter said to him, “Your money perish with you, because you thought that the gift of God could be purchased with money! You have neither part nor portion in this matter, for your heart is not right in the sight of God. Repent therefore of this your wickedness, and pray God if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you. For I see that you are poisoned by bitterness and bound by iniquity.”
Then one of them, named Agabus, stood up and showed by the Spirit that there was going to be a great famine throughout all the world, which also happened in the days of Claudius Caesar.
As they ministered to the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Now separate to Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”
Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.

faqs.question: Does “act like men” only apply to males?
faqs.answer: No—God is looking for courageous believers, male or female.

faqs.question: Did Paul ever backslide?
faqs.answer: No—he stood firm through every hardship.

faqs.question: Why did Jesus allow Satan to sift Peter?
faqs.answer: To toss him, while Jesus prayed his faith would not fail.

faqs.question: Is Jesus praying for us?
faqs.answer: Yes—he always lives to make intercession.

faqs.question: Is getting saved the end of change?
faqs.answer: No—we need more conversion to grow.

faqs.question: Did the apostles have power before Pentecost?
faqs.answer: Yes—they healed and cast out demons before the baptism of the Holy Ghost.

faqs.question: Do all speak in tongues?
faqs.answer: No—but Paul said forbid not to speak in tongues.

faqs.question: Did God confirm the apostles or the word?
Are healings and miracles for today?
faqs.answer: Yes—he says God is no respecter of persons.

faqs.question: Is America doomed?
faqs.answer: No—there are many more than ten righteous in America.
